# Wall-time budgets in seconds, one row per labeled verification stage.
# Linux columns name CPU classes mapped below to exact /proc/cpuinfo model
# names. Each stage/class budget is the maximum of at least its 20 most recent
# recorded runs plus 10%, rounded up to 5 s. The prior 10 s floor remains,
# rather than coming from the 2026-10-13 ruling; it can affect only stages
# whose measured maximum is below about 9 s. .github/recompute-time-budgets.py
# applies the rule to the stage times in CI logs; the Linux columns were last
# recomputed on 2026-10-21 over the 50 most recent runs of each stage and class
# (research/investigations/test-economy/time-budgets.md, "Recomputing the Linux
# budgets"). A cell with fewer than 20 runs of its class keeps its value, except
# in a column the owner added (see xeon-8573c below).
# A model with fewer than 20 runs has no column unless the owner adds one. An
# unmapped model uses the stage's largest Linux class budget and is reported by
# name. Unsampled rows
# retain the former Linux values until per-CPU runs are recorded in
# research/investigations/test-economy/time-budgets.md.
#
# macos values remain reported references: overruns are report-only, and so are
# the stages named in WHITEFOOT_BUDGET_REPORT_ONLY (see AGENTS.md "Checks").
# Linux and Windows overruns fail the final CI verdict; a missing row for the host fails
# on every host. run-check.pl preserves the command's status and records these
# results when WHITEFOOT_TIME_BUDGET_RECORD is set. Without a record it prints
# the comparison only. "-" marks a stage that does not run on that host.
# Windows values retain their existing rule: 1.25 times the recorded maximum,
# rounded up to 5 s, with a 10 s floor, or an owner-set value. AGENTS.md "Checks"
# states how to judge an overrun; budget raises need the owner's decision.
# Windows raises keep the 10 s increment for the stage and its group, if any.

cpu epyc-7763  AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor
cpu epyc-9v74  AMD EPYC 9V74 80-Core Processor
cpu epyc-9v45  AMD EPYC 9V45 96-Core Processor
# xeon-8573c was added by the owner on 2026-10-13 with fewer than the 20 runs a
# class needs. A row with 20 or more runs on this CPU follows the rule like any
# class: the unit group's rows, recomputed on 2026-10-21 from the CPU's own runs,
# and the other gate rows with enough runs, recomputed with
# .github/recompute-time-budgets.py. With fewer, the value is the larger of the
# row's largest recomputed class value and, where a run on this CPU was found,
# that run's time by the rule above (one compute-regression run for the compute
# rows; no run for the others). Only performance-baseline-compiler rises above
# the largest class. Evidence:
# research/investigations/test-economy/time-budgets.md.
# performance-candidate-compiler is 145 s for every Linux class, set by the
# owner on 2026-10-13 (it was 130 s).
cpu xeon-8573c INTEL(R) XEON(R) PLATINUM 8573C

label                           epyc-7763  epyc-9v74  epyc-9v45  xeon-8573c  macos  windows

# proof.yml: the Lean model's sentence coverage (building and running its
# checker), the build of its model, proofs and conformance harness, and its run
# over the conformance cases. Provisional until 20 runs are recorded: 1.5 times
# the first run of the stage's current content, rounded up to 5 s, under the
# 10 s floor (coverage 2.6 s, build 16.5 s, conformance run 0.9 s).

# sanitizers.yml: the corpus target under one sanitizer, building its test
# binary, as one conformance shard of three or the rest of the target.
# Provisional until 20 runs are recorded on a class: 1.5 times the first run's
# slowest job (conformance 276 s, programs 315 s, on epyc-7763). The two
# conformance rows of epyc-7763 follow the rule since 2026-10-21 (39 and 50
# runs); epyc-9v74 and epyc-9v45 have 10 to 16 runs of them and keep 415 s,
# and xeon-8573c, with 5, takes the epyc-7763 value (its own runs give less).
# The programs rows have fewer than 20 runs on every class and stay as they were.
